title: Bulk New-ADUser creation
brief: HR just sent a CSV of 12 new hires starting Monday. Create all accounts in OU=Users, set temporary passwords, force change at next logon, and verify — without clicking through ADUC 12 times.

commands.out:
Name              Department
----              ----------
A. Rivera         Finance
J. Okafor         IT
M. Chen           HR

commands.cmd: Get-ADUser -Filter * -SearchBase 'OU=Users,DC=lab,DC=local' -Properties Department | Group-Object Department | Select-Object Name, Count
Get-ADUser -Identity arivera -Properties PasswordExpired | Select-Object SamAccountName, PasswordExpired
# spot check one account can authenticate (test with runas or wait for Monday)
Write-Host "Created $($users.Count) accounts; all flagged for password change at logon"

title: Log triage: failed logons with Get-WinEvent
brief: The morning ticket says 'possible brute force against the DC last night.' Triage the Security log: pull event 4625s, rank source IPs, and decide whether to escalate.

commands.cmd: $parsed | Group-Object IP | Select-Object Name, Count | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 | Format-Table
$parsed | Where-Object IP -eq '203.0.113.44' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Time | Measure-Object -Minimum -Maximum | Select-Object Minimum, Maximum
# 121 failures in ~3.5h from one external IP against 'administrator' = brute force pattern
Write-Warning 'ESCALATE: brute-force from 203.0.113.44 locked out administrator; block IP at pfSense and open incident IR-2026-1042'
commands.out: WARNING: ESCALATE: brute-force from 203.0.113.44 locked out administrator; block IP at pfSense and open incident IR-2026-1042

title: DNS diagnosis with Test-NetConnection
brief: Nobody in the office can reach intranet.lab.local, but the internet works. Isolate the fault: local resolver, DNS server, or the record itself.

commands.out: Resolve-DnsName : intranet.lab.local : DNS name does not exist

commands.cmd: # client points at pfSense (192.168.10.1), not the DC — suspect forwarder issue; test the DC directly

commands.out:
Name                         Type   TTL   Section    IPAddress
----                         ----   ---   -------    ---------
intranet.lab.local             A      3600  Answer     192.168.20.25

commands.cmd: # record EXISTS on the DC — the fault is between client and DC, i.e. the pfSense forwarder

commands.out:
Server:  pfSense.lab.local
Address:  192.168.10.1
*** pfSense.lab.local can't find intranet.lab.local: Non-existent domain

commands.cmd: # pfSense DNS forwarder is not forwarding lab.local to the DC — fix: add domain override for lab.local -> 192.168.20.10
Write-Host 'Fix: pfSense Services > DNS Resolver > Domain Overrides: lab.local -> 192.168.20.10; then re-test'
commands.out: Fix: pfSense Services > DNS Resolver > Domain Overrides: lab.local -> 192.168.20.10; then re-test

Name                         Type   TTL   Section    IPAddress
----                         ----   ---   -------    ---------
intranet.lab.local             A      3600  Answer     192.168.20.25

title: Disk cleanup and management
brief: LAB-DC01's C: drive is at 91%. Find what's eating the space, clean safely, and extend the volume — without rebooting the DC.

commands.cmd: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Directory | ForEach-Object { $s=(Get-ChildItem $_.FullName -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum; [pscustomobject]@{Dir=$_.Name; GB=[math]::Round($s/1GB,1)} } | Sort-Object GB -Descending | Select-Object -First 5
commands.out:
Dir            GB
---            --
Windows       38.2
inetpub       12.6
Users          8.4
Program Files  6.1

commands.cmd: Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub\logs -Recurse -File | Measure-Object Length -Sum | Select-Object @{n='GB';e={[math]::Round($_.Sum/1GB,2)}}, Count
# IIS logs: safe to trim. Keep 30 days, delete the rest.
Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub\logs -Recurse -File | Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) | Remove-Item -Force -WhatIf | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
cleanmgr /sageset:1  # (opens UI once to define the set; then...)
vssadmin list shadows | Select-String 'Shadow Copy Volume' | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

commands.out: Successfully resized the shadow copy storage association

commands.cmd: # 8.9% -> 21.4% with zero downtime. Long-term fix: extend the VHD + volume, and cap IIS log retention.

title: Service recovery: Print Spooler crash loop
brief: The file server's Print Spooler keeps crashing every few minutes, and the helpdesk queue is filling. Diagnose, stabilize, and set recovery so it heals itself next time.

commands.cmd: Get-Service Spooler | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
commands.out:
Name    Status  StartType
----    ------  ---------
Spooler  Stopped Automatic

commands.cmd: Start-Service Spooler; Start-Sleep 5; Get-Service Spooler | Select-Object Status
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=7034; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddHours(-2)} | Select-Object -First 3 TimeCreated, Message
commands.out:
TimeCreated          Message
-----------          -------
10/7/2026 1:42:03 PM The Print Spooler service terminated unexpectedly...
10/7/2026 1:36:51 PM The Print Spooler service terminated unexpectedly...

commands.cmd: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; ProviderName='PrintService'; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddHours(-2)} -MaxEvents 5 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message
commands.out:
TimeCreated          Id Message
-----------          -- -------
10/7/2026 1:42:01 PM 372  The print spooler failed to load plug-in module C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64\3\BADPRINT.dll

commands.cmd: # culprit: a bad third-party print driver module. Stop spooler, clear the driver store entry, restart.
Start-Service Spooler; Get-Service Spooler | Select-Object Status
sc.exe failure Spooler reset= 86400 actions= restart/60000/restart/60000/reboot/60000
# recovery policy set: restart twice, then reboot the box. Verify in services.msc > Spooler > Recovery tab.
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=7036; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddMinutes(-10)} | Where-Object Message -like '*Spooler*running*' | Select-Object -First 1 TimeCreated

title: Network diagnosis flow: ipconfig to root cause
brief: A workstation reports 'no internet.' Walk the full diagnosis flow: link, IP, gateway, DNS, beyond — and find which layer is broken.

commands.cmd: ipconfig /all | Select-String 'IPv4|DHCP Enabled|Default Gateway|DNS Servers' | Select-Object -First 6
commands.out:
DHCP Enabled. . . . . . . . . . . : Yes
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 169.254.87.12(Preferred)
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . :

commands.cmd: # 169.254.x.x = APIPA. The client got NO DHCP address. Layer check: is it even on the right switch?

commands.out:
Name   Status LinkSpeed
----   ------ ---------
Ethernet Up     10 Gbps

commands.cmd: # link is UP but no DHCP and no gateway ping -> DHCP server unreachable or scope exhausted; check from the DC side
Get-DhcpServerv4ScopeStatistics -ComputerName lab-dc01.lab.local -ScopeId 192.168.10.0 | Select-Object Free, InUse, PercentageInUse
# scope EXHAUSTED: 101 leases, 0 free. Someone is squatting — check for the rogue.
Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ComputerName lab-dc01.lab.local -ScopeId 192.168.10.0 | Group-Object HostName | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object -First 3 Name, Count
# lab-test-old holds 38 leases (stale reservations). Reclaim: shorten lease to 8h, delete stale leases, expand scope to .50-.250.

title: Linux service triage: systemctl + journalctl
brief: lab-linux01's status page (IL27-TL-08) stopped responding on port 8080. Triage from the shell: is the container up, is Docker up, what do the logs say?

commands.cmd: # container is UP but curl gets 000 = connection refused. Check what the container is actually listening on.
# port IS listening. So the proxy accepts but the app drops it — check container logs.

commands.out:
2026/10/07 14:02:11 [emerg] 1#1: open() "/etc/nginx/conf.d/custom.conf" failed (2: No such file or directory)
nginx: [emerg] ... test failed

commands.cmd: # nginx died at 14:02 after a config change; docker shows Up because the proxy holds the port. Inspect the bad volume mount.
docker inspect status --format '{{json .Mounts}}' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -A2 Source

commands.out: ls: cannot access '/home/ops/status-page/conf.d/': No such file or directory

commands.cmd: # someone deleted the conf.d dir. Recreate it and restart.

commands.out: Oct 07 14:20:11 lab-linux01 dockerd[701]: ... container status restarted

commands.cmd: echo 'Root cause: deleted nginx conf.d volume; container proxy masked the failure. Fix: recreate dir + restart; add Zabbix check on HTTP 200.'
commands.out: Root cause: deleted nginx conf.d volume; container proxy masked the failure. Fix: recreate dir + restart; add Zabbix check on HTTP 200.
